rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance – criminal history screening ban
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions. They also may not refuse to rent, terminate a tenancy, demand a higher deposit or rent, or block the addition of an immediate family member based on criminal history.
rules.key_value: No criminal history inquiry or use
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley, as to current and prospective tenants.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing and Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back in per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units where existing tenants seek to sublet or add or replace roommates.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemptions for lifetime sex offender applicants, limited public housing/Section 8 exemptions, owner move-back rental agreements (BMC 13.76.130 A.9), and existing-tenant sublets or roommate additions/replacements.

rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation; civil damages including actual damages or three times one month's rent; punitive damages; attorneys' fees and costs; injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.conflict_note: The page states only the City Council passage date (April 14, 2020). The effective date is not given.

rules.title: Fair Chance Ordinance – written notice and opportunity to respond; required applicant notice
rules.requirement: A landlord who takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history must give written notice and an opportunity to respond. Housing providers must also post the Notice to Rental Applicants and Tenants prominently on application materials, websites, and frequently visited locations.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords in Berkeley taking adverse action based on criminal history, and housing providers distributing application materials.
rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the Fair Chance Ordinance, including owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when adverse action is based on criminal history. Ordinance exemptions apply (lifetime sex offenders, limited public housing/Section 8, owner move-back agreements, sublets/roommates).

rules.penalty: Administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation, plus civil damages, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history (such as refusing to offer a lease, refusing to add a family member, etc.), the landlord is required to provide the applicant/tenant with written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.conflict_note: The effective date is not stated on the page. Only the passage date (April 14, 2020) is given.
